 |deck=The current state of EDFM's content, its strongest subject areas, and the work still in progress.
}}

The '''Elite Dangerous Field Manual''' is live, publicly readable, and under active development. Coverage varies by subject, so gameplay-facing articles use review and source-status information to show how thoroughly their content has been checked.

== How EDFM coverage is organized ==
EDFM separates factual reference material from practical procedures.

{{Field note|'''Game Reference''' explains what something is and how its own mechanics work. '''Field Procedures''' explain how to complete a task.}}

Reference articles retain enough context to answer the obvious questions about their subject, then link to the related mechanic or procedure for details. Field Procedures may be long when a task requires substantial preparation, ordered steps, warnings, and troubleshooting.

See [[Elite Dangerous Field Manual:Editorial Policy#Topic ownership and page scope|Topic ownership and page scope]] for the full content rule.

== Content snapshot ==
=== Engineering ===
'''Status: Substantial coverage; active architecture review'''

Engineering is one of EDFM's most developed subject areas. Current coverage includes:

* ship and Odyssey Engineers;
* Engineer locations and unlock requirements;
* direct referrals and referral chains;
* ship Engineering grades and blueprint availability;
* Odyssey suit and weapon modifications;
* Experimental Effects;
* Engineering Materials; and
* practical Engineer-unlock guidance.

Engineer articles keep Engineer-specific facts separate from full unlock procedures, blueprint mechanics, material-acquisition guides, and general Engineering strategy.

See [[Engineering]], [[Engineers]], [[Engineer Unlock Guide]], [[Engineering Blueprints]], [[Experimental Effects]], and [[Elite Dangerous Field Manual:Engineering Architecture|Engineering Architecture]].

=== New and returning commanders ===
'''Status: In development'''

[[Start Here]], the [[New Commander Roadmap]], and the [[Returning Commander Overview]] provide separate entry paths for commanders learning the game and those returning after an extended absence.

These routes focus on orientation and useful next steps rather than reproducing every linked subject in full.

=== Field Procedures ===
'''Status: Expanding'''

[[Field Procedures]] are task-focused guides covering preparation, required equipment, ordered actions, common mistakes, troubleshooting, and expected results. Procedure pages retain useful detail when it directly helps a commander complete the task.

=== Game Reference ===
'''Status: Expanding'''

[[Game Reference]] contains quick-reference information such as requirements, values, specifications, capabilities, locations, and comparisons. Reference pages explain their own subjects and link to Field Procedures for complete workflows.

=== Ships and Equipment ===
'''Status: Partial coverage'''

[[Ships and Equipment]] covers ships, vehicles, modules, stock specifications, equipment roles, and directly associated mechanics. Individual ship and vehicle articles remain separate from build guides, Engineering strategy, and activity walkthroughs.

=== Odyssey ===
'''Status: Partial coverage'''

[[Odyssey]] includes substantial Engineer information and growing coverage of suits, handheld weapons, settlements, missions, materials, stealth, infiltration, Surface Conflict Zones, and other on-foot activities.

=== Powerplay ===
'''Status: Needs expansion and continuing review'''

[[Powerplay]] requires current mechanics-focused reference material and practical procedures. Older explanations need careful version checks because the system has undergone major revisions.

=== Colonisation ===
'''Status: In development'''

[[Colonisation]] covers system expansion, construction planning, project supply, facility requirements, and system development. Detailed operational tasks belong in linked procedures rather than a single oversized overview.

=== Operations ===
'''Status: Needs expansion'''

[[Operations]] covers newer Live gameplay and equipment introduced after Live and Legacy diverged. This area also affects older subjects when newer modules, blueprints, or activities have version-specific restrictions or capabilities.

=== Lore and history ===
'''Status: Needs expansion'''

Lore and historical material belongs on EDFM when it helps explain a location, faction, event, mechanic, or activity that a commander may encounter. EDFM does not attempt to reproduce an exhaustive fictional encyclopedia.

== What a review status means ==
A page can contain useful information and still require further review. A reviewed article, where applicable:

* uses current sources;
* distinguishes confirmed facts from recommendations and community observations;
* identifies meaningful Live and Legacy differences;
* avoids presenting obsolete requirements as current;
* resolves conflicting information where reasonably possible;
* explains important game quirks rather than repeating misleading interface text; and
* cites sources for factual claims.

See [[Elite Dangerous Field Manual:Editorial Policy]] and [[Elite Dangerous Field Manual:Verification Policy]] for the full standards.

== Current priorities ==
Current work focuses on:

* expanding incomplete subject coverage;
* improving navigation between reference subjects, mechanics, and procedures;
* replacing incomplete drafts with verified reader-ready material;
* checking existing claims against current game behaviour; and
* distinguishing Live, Legacy, Odyssey, and historical mechanics where necessary.

The detailed article queue is maintained at [[Elite Dangerous Field Manual:Pages Needing Review|Pages Needing Review]] so individual research and verification tasks are not duplicated here.

== Contributing ==
Useful contributions include correcting inaccurate information, adding missing procedures, expanding incomplete reference pages, providing current in-game verification, documenting version-specific behaviour, and improving explanations that are difficult to follow.

A well-documented correction or firsthand verification of one mechanic is useful even when the contributor does not have broad expertise in the surrounding subject.

Before making substantial additions, see [[Elite Dangerous Field Manual:Contributing|Contributing]], [[Elite Dangerous Field Manual:Editorial Policy|Editorial Policy]], and [[Elite Dangerous Field Manual:Pages Needing Review|Pages Needing Review]].
